what_happened: On a multi-lane highway, the route said RIGHT and the recorded path stayed in the ego's lane or bore right. Instead, the policy steered left toward the next lane (orange path) at about 4 m/s. Its front corner hit actor 41, which was driving alongside in that left lane.

After handoff the ego drove straight on the highway at about 8 m/s but drifted left, about 0.9 m off the human's path, into the next lane. Its front-left corner hit actor 33 as that car came alongside in the left lane, even though the route command had just changed to RIGHT.

The ego was moving slowly (about 4 m/s) on a multi-lane highway. Its planned path veered left of the recorded trajectory (about 2 m off), so it drifted across the lane line into the left lane. Vehicle 29 had come up from behind in that lane, and the ego's front-left struck it at 11.6 s.

On a multi-lane highway with no lead vehicle, the ego stayed in its lane (0.3 m from the recorded path) but slowed from 13.6 to 10 m/s. Actor 14 passed it on the right and merged left into the ego's lane, clipping the ego's front-right corner. A rear contact was also logged during the run.

The ego was going straight in its lane on a highway and slowing gently (13.6 to 10 m/s) while staying within 0.4 m of the recorded path. Actor 14 came up from behind on the right, passed alongside and cut left into the ego's lane, clipping the ego's front-right corner.

The ego slowed to about 4 m/s behind the white truck (actor 2), then drifted left into the next lane over, even though the command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT. Its front hit vehicle 41, which was travelling in that left lane and was right beside the ego at 7.7 s.

On a straight multi-lane highway, the ego slowed from 4.6 to 3.4 m/s and wandered left, ending about 2 m left of the recorded path, instead of following its planned route line one lane to the right. At 11.6 s its left side hit actor 29, a small vehicle that had come up alongside in the left lane, as a lateral collision.

Cruising straight at about 8 m/s on a multi-lane freeway, the ego drifted about 0.9 m left of the recorded path, into the lane edge where actor 33 was passing on the left. The ego's front-left clipped actor 33 at 6.6 s. The lead vehicle was more than 25 m ahead, so braking for a lead was not the issue.

On a multi-lane highway in the rain, the ego steered left out of its lane even though the command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT, and the recorded path stayed to the right. Moving at about 4 m/s, it cut into the left lane and its front hit actor 41, which was alongside it in that lane.

On a multi-lane highway, the ego was crawling at about 4 m/s, far below traffic speed and about 68 m behind where the human driver was. It also drifted about 2 m left toward the lane line, and a small actor (id 2) passing on its left made side contact at 11.6 s. The ego's slow speed and its drift into the next lane's space put it in the passing vehicle's path; nothing was close ahead of it.

Actor 66 came up behind the ego and was already overlapping its rear by 3.7s, before the policy took over (the rear-collision flag fires then). By 4.7s it had pushed further into the ego's box, so a lateral collision was recorded at the very moment of handoff (4.7s), while the ego was still cruising at about 4.2 m/s on the logged path with the lead car 11 m ahead.

The ego was going straight in its lane, slowing from about 12 to 10 m/s and staying within 0.3 m of the recorded path. Actor 14 came up from behind on the right, passed it, and cut left into the ego's lane, so the rear of actor 14 clipped the ego's front-right corner. The ego was also rear-ended at some point in the run, so this was an actor hitting the ego rather than the ego driving into anything.

Actor 66, following in the ego's lane, ran into the ego's rear (rear contact already at 3.7s) while the ego was still replaying the recorded trajectory and the lead car was pulling away. At the 4.7s handoff the overlap had deepened and was counted as a side collision, so the 'at-fault' flag is an artifact; the policy had no chance to act.

On a straight multi-lane freeway at about 8 m/s, the policy's path bent left toward the next lane while actor 33 was overtaking in that lane. By 6.6 s the ego had moved about 0.9 m left of the recorded path, and its front-left corner hit actor 33 as the car came alongside.

On a straight multi-lane highway at about 17 m/s, replayed actors 28 and then 31 came up from behind in the ego's lane and drove straight through its box. The rear contact with 28 at 4.1s happened before the policy took over at 4.6s. By 5.1s actor 31 overlaps the ego and 28 has passed through to sit just ahead, so the "front" collision is a side effect of these non-reactive actors overlapping the ego, which stayed within 0.1 m of the recorded human path the whole time.

The ego followed the recorded human path (0.0 m off) behind truck 2 in the same lane, and its box was already touching the truck at 3.7s (collision_any = 1 in that frame), which is before the policy took over at 4.7s. The front collision with truck 2 happened during log replay, probably because the actor or ego box is too large for the real gap (2.9 m), so it was flagged the moment the policy took over and the policy never really drove.

The ego stayed in its lane and sped up from 4.5 to 6.7 m/s. The recorded human trajectory, by contrast, drifted left. Actor 56 came up from behind on the ego's left, and at 7.2 s the two had a sideswipe (lateral) contact while the ego was about 1.4 m from the recorded path, with no clear steer by the ego into 56.

Actor 66 came up behind the ego and was already in rear contact by 3.7 s, before the policy took over at 4.7 s. At handoff the ego was exactly on the recorded path, slowing gently with a growing gap to the car ahead. The contact still in progress was then scored as an at-fault side collision.

The ego was still replaying the recorded human trajectory (0 m off the recording) in slow traffic. Its box was already overlapping the lead car 12 in the same lane by 3.7 s, when collision_front first registers. The policy only took over at 4.7 s, the same moment the failure was counted, so this looks like an artifact of the scenario setup or actor-track overlap in the log rather than a decision by the policy.

Before handoff the ego was replaying the recorded trajectory (0.0 m off the recording) at a steady 8 m/s, closing on actor 1 ahead from 7.6 m to 0 m. A front collision was already flagged at 3.6 s, and by the 4.6 s handoff the ego box sat completely on top of actor 1. The camera shows no vehicle in that spot, so actor 1 is probably a badly placed or ghost reconstruction, and the failure was scored at the first moment the policy took over, before it could do anything.

The ego was still replaying the recorded human drive at a steady ~8 m/s. Its box already overlapped lead actor 1 from 2.6 s on (collision_front Per-Ts = 1 in every frame, gap only 2–3 m), so the collision was flagged the instant the policy took over at 4.6 s. This is a log or bounding-box overlap artifact, not anything the policy did.

The ego was still replaying the recorded human trajectory (0.0 m off the log), and the collision happened at 4.6 s, the same moment as handoff, so the policy never controlled the car. Lead actor 1's track closed in on the ego's logged path at a steady 2.6 m/s until the two boxes overlapped (camera smeared at 3.6 s, full overlap at 4.6 s). This points to an inconsistent actor track in the reconstruction, not a driving mistake.

On a multi-lane highway with the command STRAIGHT (RIGHT at the end), the ego sped up from 4.5 to 6.7 m/s and followed a planned path that veered left, away from the recorded route. It drifted into the adjacent left lane and its front hit vehicle 56, which was travelling alongside in that lane. The rear contact came afterwards.
